lessonRecap.stringValue: The Philippines is an archipelago. Water separates islands but also provides routes between them. Boat remains found in Butuan give evidence of early boatbuilding and water travel. Archaeologists study the wood and the way parts join. Butuan boats were built from wooden planks. Builders used skilled ways of joining parts, including pegs and lashings. Seafaring needs knowledge of water, weather, routes and the boat. People learned through experience and teaching. Archaeologists record where boat parts are found and how they relate to nearby objects. Their place in the ground can be important evidence.
